raw_response:
I've been farming cotton here in Quzhou for forty years now. My five mu is all cotton — that's what this land knows best, and the soil here suits it. With high school education, I read the input bags, I listen to the extension station when they come through, and I keep notes on what worked each year.

This year I'll plant Bt hybrid cotton — the bollworm-resistant kind. Seed is about 80 yuan per mu but it saves me three or four pesticide sprays against bollworm, which is worth it. I've been using Bt varieties for years; going back to traditional would be foolish.

For fertilizer, cotton is hungry but needs balance. Last year I put about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu split across base and topdressing, and yields were decent around 280 kg seed cotton. I'll do similar — maybe 20 kg N because fertilizer prices dropped a bit and an extra kilo of nitrogen is cheaper than losing bolls. Phosphorus 8 kg as base, potassium 10 kg because cotton really needs K for boll filling and my soil tests showed K was getting low. I'll use a compound 15-15-15 at planting (about 40 kg/mu) and urea for topdressing at squaring and flowering.

Irrigation — I have my own well, which is good because rainfall here is unreliable. I'll water at planting for emergence, then at squaring, flowering, and boll development. Four times usually. If July is dry, maybe a fifth.

Pesticides — even with Bt, I still need to spray for aphids, spider mites, and plant bugs. Bt doesn't cover those. I'll plan on 5 sprays: aphids early, mites mid-season, plant bugs during flowering, plus a defoliant before picking. Neighbors who skip sprays on sucking pests lose yield.

Tillage — I plough deep every year before planting to break up compaction and bury residue. Rotary alone isn't enough for cotton roots.

Yield target: 290 kg seed cotton per mu. Last year 280, weather was okay. With the extra potassium and careful management I think 290 is realistic.
